summary: Iterative median-split tree builder over an array of 6-coordinate axis-aligned boxes (stride 8 dwords). For each output node it scans the input box array, selects the box whose split-key value is greatest (two scan variants differ in start offset and in a positivity filter on the preceding coordinate), copies the 6 box coordinates into the node, picks the widest axis by comparing scaled extents, bisects that axis at the midpoint (writing midpoint+1 as a split marker), and hands both resulting halves to GridOccupancyBoundingBoxScan. The loop advances two tree positions per node until the count reaches a4.

local_names.a1: grid/occupancy structure passed through to GridOccupancyBoundingBoxScan
local_names.a2: base of the box array; each element is 8 dwords with a 6-coordinate box at its head
local_names.a4: exclusive upper bound on the box index
local_names.v6: output node pointer (a2 + 32*a3 + 12), advanced 8 dwords per node
local_names.v7: selected source box pointer within the scanned range
local_names.v8: largest split-key value found by the scan
local_names.v12: chosen split axis (0 = x, 1 = y, 2 = z)

operations.description: Alias result = a3 and v5 = a2 before any processing.
Guard on a3 < a4: the tree-building loop only runs while there is at least one box to process.
Initialize the node index v19 = 2*a3 and the output node pointer v6 = a2 + 32*a3 + 12, i.e. the (a3)-th stride-32 element offset by 12 bytes.
Outer while(1) node loop; each iteration resets the selected box v7 and best key v8 to 0.
Branch on v19 > a4: the upper-range scan variant starts at a2+24 and steps 8 dwords, while the a4-reachable variant starts at a2+28 and additionally requires the preceding coordinate *(v9-1) > 0.
do-while scan over result (= a3) candidates; picks v7 as the box whose scanned key *v9 is greater than v8.
if (!v7) break: when no box beats the initial zero key the outer loop terminates.
Copy the selected box's six coordinates into the output node: node[-2]=src[1], node[0]=src[3], node[2]=src[5], node[-3]=src[0], node[-1]=src[2], node[1]=src[4].
Axis selection by scaled extent: v11 = 12*(src[3]-src[2]) for y; if 16*(src[1]-src[0]) > v11 choose x (v12=0); if 8*(src[5]-src[4]) > v11 choose z (v12=2); otherwise keep y (v12=1).
Bisect the chosen axis at its midpoint: x -> src[1]=mid, node[-3]=mid+1; y -> src[3]=mid, node[-1]=mid+1; z -> src[5]=mid, node[1]=mid+1. The midpoint+1 values act as split markers in the node.
GridOccupancyBoundingBoxScan(a1, v7) on the first half of the split box.
GridOccupancyBoundingBoxScan(a1, v6 - 3) on the second half of the split box (the copied node).
Advance the walk: v19 += 2, result = a3 + 1, v6 += 8, and ++a3.
Terminate the outer loop once ++a3 >= a4; v5 is reset to a2 each iteration.
Return the final index (a3+1 of the last processed node, or a3 when nothing was processed); invoked from RenderBufferSetup.

clean_pseudocode: int BuildMedianSplitOccupancyTree(int grid, int* boxes, int first, int end) {
if (index > 0) { int* p = (int*)((char*)boxes + 24); int n = first;
do { if (*p > best) { src = p - 6; best = *p; } p += 8; } while (--n); }
} else if (index > 0) { int* p = (int*)((char*)boxes + 28); int n = first;
do { if (*p > best && *(p-1) > 0) { src = p - 7; best = *p; } p += 8; } while (--n); }
else if (axis == 1) { int m = (src[2]+src[3])/2; src[3]=m; node[-1]=m+1; }
unresolved: The two scan variants (v19 > a4 starting at +24 with no extra filter, vs the a4-reachable variant starting at +28 with the *(v9-1) > 0 filter) are not otherwise explained; the positivity filter's meaning is unknown.
The exact layout semantics of a1 and its role in GridOccupancyBoundingBoxScan are supplied by the callee, not this function.
The midpoint+1 split markers written into the node are presumed to be consumed by GridOccupancyBoundingBoxScan; this is unverified here.
The 12/16/8 scaling factors on the axis extents are literal weights whose geometric intent (aspect compensation) is not proven.
